title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 303–305, section 'X_{ρ,σ}'): Grothendieck is studying a scheme of solutions of the 'loop equation' in GL2/SL2 over a base S. On p. 303 he states that the scheme of triples (ξ,η,μ) with det ξ = det η = 1, ξ = η ε_1(μ−1), Tr(ξρ) = Tr ρ and Tr(ησ) = Tr σ is isomorphic, via projection to ξ, to the scheme of matrices ξ = (A B; C D) with det ξ = 1, C + wD + vB = w and D invertible. He also announces an isomorphism (39) from the group scheme B'_0 = {u = (μ λ; 0 1)} (an affine 'ax+b' group, a twisted Borel) onto this solution scheme, given by u ↦ ([u,ρ], [u,σ], det u). On this page he makes (39) explicit.

He takes ρ = (0 1; v w), so det ρ = −v, and computes the commutator [u,ρ] = uρu^{-1}ρ^{-1}. Grouping u^{-1}ρ^{-1} = (1/μ)(1 −λ; 0 μ)·(−1/v)(w −1; −v 0) gives
ξ = (1/μ)( μ² + λ(−vλ + w(μ−1)) , λ ; −vλ + w(μ−1) , 1 ).

He then takes σ = (0 −1; v' w') with v' = −v and w' = 1 − w, which encodes the constraint linking ρ and σ in his set-up. The same computation gives
η = (1/μ)( μ² + λ(−vλ + (w−1)(μ−1)) , λ ; −vλ + (w−1)(μ−1) , 1 ).
The third component is μ = det u. This is the summary (46).

Reading off the entries B = λ/μ and D = 1/μ ((47)) inverts the map: μ = 1/D, λ = B/D, so u = (1/D B/D; 0 1) ((48)). This exhibits the inverse of the isomorphism B'_0 → X_{ρ,σ} and matches formula (43), μ = 1/D, from p. 303. The next page does the same from η (S = B, U = D) and then moves on to the general equation [α,ρ] = [β,σ] ε_1(μ^{-1}).
errors: No computational errors found. Every intermediate product checks out.
Check: det ξ = (1/μ²)[(−vλ² + wλμ + μ² − wλ) − λ(−vλ + wμ − w)] = 1, and likewise det η = 1.
Check: ξ = η·(1 0; μ−1 1). So with ε_1(t) = (1 0; t 1), relation (41) ξ = η ε_1(μ−1) is satisfied, as it should be.
Minor: the trace conditions Tr(ξρ) = Tr ρ are not re-verified on this page; they hold implicitly because the map is announced as an isomorphism onto the solution scheme.

ideas.what: Explicit parametrization of a solution scheme of a commutator/loop equation in GL2 by an affine (ax+b) group scheme B'_0, via u ↦ ([u,ρ],[u,σ],det u), with explicit inverse μ = 1/D, λ = B/D.
ideas.modern_name: Explicit commutator maps on GL2 / torsor parametrization of a fibre of a character-variety-type equation (relative to the free group on two generators)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard matrix computation; the general context of SL2 character varieties and trace coordinates goes back to Fricke–Klein, with modern treatments by Culler–Shalen, Goldman and others
ideas.where_published: Not in published texts. Related themes (Teichmüller tower, loops on P^1 minus 3 points) appear in Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche, but this computation does not.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a correct, routine explicit matrix computation verifying and inverting an announced isomorphism (39) between a Borel-type group scheme and a solution scheme. It contains no new conceptual content beyond the surrounding section.
transcription_corrections: Line 3 of the [u,ρ] computation: the top-left entry is v²λ² − vμ² − vwλμ + vwλ (μ written over an erasure). The bottom-left entry is v²λ − vwμ + vw; the crossed-out text before it is a deleted attempt.
The left margin reads 'on pose σ = (0 −1; v' w')' with 'où v' = −v' and 'où w' = 1−w'.
After (46), 'μ = det u' is followed by a crossed-out word. The right-margin word next to η reads approximately 'arbitraires' (presumably λ, μ arbitrary), but this is uncertain.
The line before (47) reads approximately 'donc, si ξ = (A B; C D)'.
